summary: Input (contract 13) and camera (contract 14) replace the B0a stubs. SteeringInput: touch floating stick (Screen.dpi clamped to [120, 560], 160 when 0; dead zone 0.05 in, leash 0.20 in with the anchor following), steering finger = first touch that begins while none steers and whose press point hits no Selectable (EventSystem.RaycastAll at the press frame, never IsPointerOverGameObject), other touches ignored for their whole lifetime, left-button mouse drag with the same rules, hover steering that arms after 8 px and steers toward the cursor only beyond 2.5 u (converted with the camera scale), keyboard arrows / WASD in 8 directions, device precedence (pointer drag > held key > hover, most recent wins), Escape / Android back per state (Playing: SetPaused(!IsPaused); Results: ToMenu; Menu: UiRoot.HandleBack, which B4 deduplicates per frame), drop and re-anchor on SessionStarted and on PausedChanged. It writes HumanController.Desired from deliberate input only; DefaultExecutionOrder(-200) so the write reaches GameDirector's ready gate and the sim in the same frame. CameraRig: main camera created at runtime with the contract 14 settings and UniversalAdditionalCameraData, DefaultExecutionOrder(100), 18 u wide in portrait / 20 u high in landscape, exact critically damped follow (half-life 0.12 s) plus a 1.2 u lookahead smoothed by its own spring (0.35 s), chase framing clamp(1.15 x needed width, 18, 26) containing head, retraction front (RenderSparkS) and the HomeArrow target (GridQueries.NearestOwned, cached per tick) with 1.5 u padding, eased in with a 0.25 s half-life and back to 18 u over 0.6 s (smoothstep), attract drift on the leading bot (10 % hysteresis), death beat hold on the elimination point, results hold with a slight zoom out (x1.1), clamp to 4 u beyond the arena. Snap on a new session, drift on an attract restart. The pure math is factored into public static functions with 30 EditMode test cases; 4 PlayMode tests drive virtual keyboard, mouse and touchscreen through the Input System test fixture. Verified in the Windows player with DevShot (plus a -camdebug overlay): every checkpoint keeps the human in view, CutDroplets keeps the front and home target in view, Caught holds on the splash, results hold with zoom out; zero exceptions in player.log.

The camera GameObject is now named 'CameraRig' (no longer '(stub)'), keeps the MainCamera tag and carries the only AudioListener (added only when none exists).
contract_issues: 14 chase framing in landscape is not specified (the 18..26 u clamp is a portrait width). Implemented as one view scale: portrait width 18 x s, landscape height 20 x s, s in [1, 26/18]; the needed size accounts for both axes through the aspect ratio.

14 'the width needed to contain the head, the front and the home target': read as the view centered on the follow target (head + smoothed lookahead) that contains all three points with 1.5 u padding on every side, so a vertical spread in portrait also counts through the aspect ratio. In portrait the base view is 18 x 32 u, so the zoom rarely triggers on vertical spreads (demo: peak 20.6 u right after the first cut, 18 u at CutDroplets, about 26 u on the second chase when home is 13 u away).

14 'critically damped spring (half-life h)': implemented as the exact closed-form critically damped spring whose step response from rest covers exactly half the distance in h (damping y = 1.678347 / h). 'Eased in with a 0.25 s half-life' is a first-order exponential; 'back to 18 u over 0.6 s' is a smoothstep over 0.6 s.

13 device precedence 'the most recently active device owns Desired': a held key or a drag blocks hover; once released, hover takes Desired back only after the cursor moved 8 px again (the arming threshold reused as the activity threshold), so desk jitter cannot steal the course. Keys held when a session starts or a pause ends count as deliberate input and release the ready gate at once.

13 hover, small addition: while the cursor rests on a Selectable (pause button, leaderboard toggle) hover keeps the course instead of steering into the corner. Pure presentation of the contract rule that only Selectables block steering; remove if unwanted.

11.1 / 13 the ready gate: SteeringInput runs at DefaultExecutionOrder(-200) (before GameDirector's -100) so the first write is seen by the gate and the next tick in the same frame. The contract does not fix this order; it only removes one frame of input lag.
open_issues: Counts: EditMode InputCameraMathTests 30/30 (TestResults/B3_edit.xml, also green in a dotnet NUnit host); PlayMode SteeringInputPlayTests 4/4 on the final code (TestResults/B3_play_input.xml); BootTests 3/3 green with the B3 camera and input (TestResults/B3_play.xml). The full EditMode and PlayMode suites were not re-run by B3 (other packages are mid-edit); B3's files touch no shared code path except the camera and Desired writes.

The first PlayMode run failed Touch_FloatingStickOwnsTheFirstFingerOnly: TouchControl.press.wasPressedThisFrame did not report the press frame of a touch slot under the test fixture. Press frames are now detected by tracking touch ids down at the previous update (more robust, and it makes 'ignored for its whole lifetime' explicit); the rerun is green. Real-device touch (Android) is still unverified: no device attached. B6's device playtest (18.5) covers it.

Escape in Menu: B4's UiRoot also reads Escape itself and dedupes per frame with HandleBack, so B3 calling HandleBack is safe and acts once (PlayMode test asserts the quit panel opens and does not toggle twice).

uGUI keyboard navigation: InputSystemUIInputModule maps arrows / WASD to Navigate. If a button stays selected during play (for example after clicking pause then resume), arrows also move the UI selection. Not seen in tests; B4 may clear EventSystem.current.SetSelectedGameObject(null) when entering Playing.
The chase zoom changes the main camera's orthographicSize continuously for up to about 1 s per chase; see needs for B1 about the actor field RT size.
needs: B1 (ActorFieldCamera, perf): the RT size round((view + 1.2 u) x ppu x tierScale) shifts by up to about 11 px during the chase zoom because the 0.6 u margin is expressed in world units while ppu changes, so the actor RT is reallocated on most frames of each zoom ease (about 1 s per chase and 0.6 s after it). Suggest quantizing the RT size (for example round up to a multiple of 32 px, or allocate for the widest chase view, CameraRig.MaxChaseScale, and only grow), or expressing the margin in pixels.
B5: the main camera carries the game's only AudioListener (added by CameraRig only when none exists); Sfx already adds its own only when none exists, so nothing to change.

B6: tools/verify.ps1's PlayMode step runs every PlayMode assembly, now including PainterIO.Tests.PlayModeInput (4 tests with InputTestFixture, they set LogAssert.ignoreFailingMessages and only fail on errors logged by SteeringInput / CameraRig). PlayerProbe can pass -camdebug for framing screenshots, and the '[CameraRig] checkpoint' log lines give the framing numbers per checkpoint.
